title: Revit Project Template Governance and Use
purpose: Provide source-backed instructions for selecting, using, maintaining, and versioning governed Revit project templates without promoting draft template names or incomplete template catalogues into canonical authority.
preconditions: An approved project or discipline template has been designated for the project context.

Canonical naming, parameter, view, annotation, graphics, material, worksharing, and titleblock rules are obtained from their governing standards or registries rather than inferred from this instruction.
Any project-specific deviation is governed through the applicable standards/BEP change process.

steps.name: Select the governed template for project scope
actions: Determine whether the project requires the enterprise base template or an approved discipline-specific template.
Confirm the selected template is the current governed release for the intended Revit version and project context.
validation: The project starts from an approved template appropriate to its discipline and scope.
No ad-hoc or legacy template is treated as current without explicit governance approval.

steps.name: Verify required governed content is present
actions: Verify the template contains or references approved titleblocks, view templates, annotation styles, object styles, line styles, materials, phases, worksets where applicable, and governed project/shared parameters.
Treat missing or inconsistent content as a template-governance issue rather than silently replacing it with local project content.
validation: Required governed content is available for the intended project use.
Missing or obsolete content is logged for governed correction.

steps.name: Control template changes and versioning
actions: Make standards-level template changes only through the governed template maintenance/release process.
Record the template version/release used by the project.
Do not treat source-era filename examples or placeholder catalogue IDs as canonical naming rules.
validation: Template changes are traceable to a governed release or approved project exception.
The project can identify the template release from which it was initialized or aligned.

outputs: Project initialized or aligned to an approved Revit project template
evidence: Template validation checklist or automated inventory
governance_notes: Source template filename patterns and placeholder catalogue entries remain examples/TODOs and are not promoted.
Template content implements governing standards; the template itself does not redefine those standards.

provenance.migration_note: Normalized as L6 implementation guidance. Source placeholders and incomplete template-name/catalogue values are intentionally not canonicalized.
